idiom_name: detect -> per-format translator -> one canonical message (router plus translator table)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral skeleton: (1) a detection step reads the type specifier if the transport provides one, otherwise applies documented heuristics (root element, schema probe, field shape, file name or channel); (2) a routing table maps the detected tag to exactly one translator per source format; (3) each translator performs the complete mapping into the canonical message - field names, units, currency, dates, code lists, precision - and reports unmappable input instead of defaulting it; (4) the canonical message is validated against its versioned schema and annotated with provenance (source system, format version, translator version) before publication; (5) messages that cannot be detected, translated or validated go to an invalid-message channel carrying the original payload. Keep one responsibility per component: detection knows only tags, translators know only their own format, consumers know only the canonical form. When one logical message arrives as correlated fragments, merge them with an Aggregator before publication rather than teaching consumers about partial messages.
code_sketch:
tag = detect(raw)                     # header type specifier, else documented heuristics
translator = table[tag]               # exactly one translator per source format
if translator is None: invalid_channel(raw)     # never guess, never drop silently
canonical = translator.map(raw)       # units/currency/dates/codes normalized here
validate(canonical, canonical_schema) # versioned contract, unknown-field policy
canonical.provenance = (source, format_version, translator_version)
publish(canonical)                    # every consumer sees exactly this shape
pitfalls: Detection is the weak link: without a sender-supplied type specifier the tag is inferred from structure, field counts or the file name, and an ambiguous source is silently misrouted into a well-formed but wrong canonical message.
A translator that pre-fills defaults for missing fields turns a partner's omission into business data; absent, empty and invalid must stay distinguishable.
The canonical model drifts into the union of every producer's fields and then into the domain model; it needs a named owner and a versioned contract.
Merging correlated fragments downstream instead of before publication lets consumers observe partial messages and spreads the merge rule.

Wrong move: let a missing JSONPath value become a default -> EventBridge Pipes emits an empty string for an absent path, which can look valid downstream -> instead validate required fields after translation and quarantine missing data.

Wrong move: make one enterprise-wide DTO for unrelated bounded contexts -> the canonical model accumulates optional attributes and semantic mismatches -> instead normalize into a context-owned boundary contract and preserve each domain's meaning.

Wrong move: map only matching field names and discard the source artifact -> structural serialization can lose identity, authority, version or causality and make replay impossible -> instead retain raw input plus provenance and document every intentionally forgotten distinction.
